Full and outside off, Pujara gets this in the gap through the covers but the timing isn't that great. The batsmen come back for two.
Too straight in line, allows Kohli to pick it off his pads and clip it through square leg for a double.
Full length delivery quite close to off, blocked with the full face of the bat.

Edgy FOUR! It falls short of the slip fielder, but credit to Kohli as he plays it by taking his bottom hand off. Length ball outside off, Kohli hangs his bat and the edge is induced. It falls short of a diving Shaun Marsh and goes through him for a boundary. The 150 comes up for India with this.
Too far outside off, easy enough for VK to leave it alone.
Gets on top of the bounce and dabs this wide of point. Kohli runs the first one hard and comes back for the second.
FOUR! Good balance on that shot. Nice and still from Virat Kohli. Extremely full on off, the Indian captain drives this ever so well through mid on and finds the fence.
Change of ends for Josh Hazlewood.

Short ball angling in, on middle, Pujara has no intention to play at it so tries to duck under it. But the ball doesn't rise as much and it goes off his shoulder and lobs towards fine leg. Two leg byes taken.
Starc keeps firing it full, outside off, one more defensive shot presented by the batsman.
Comes from wide of the crease and angles in a full delivery on off, Pujara remains watchful as he defensively pushes it out in front of covers.
Comes from around the wicket on this occasion and angles in a fuller ball outside off, left alone.
Touch fuller in length, on off stump, Cheteshwar meets it with the full face.
Back of a length delivery angling across, Virat dabs it wide of point and jogs across to the other end.
Mitchell Starc replaces Josh Hazlewood.
Shortish delivery on middle and off, Che is right behind the line as he defends it right beside him on the leg side.
Back of a length outside off, it's dabbed down to third man for a comfortable single.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.

FOUR! Overpitched from Cummins and he pays the price. Just around off, Virat Kohli beautifully drives it through mid on. Head gives it a chase and makes a lazy attempt to pull it back inside the rope. Ends up conceding a boundary. Should be doing better.
Full just outside off, defended in front of the covers.
Back of a length outside off, Kohli opens the bat face and dabs it to gully.
Nice carry on that. Good length delivery in the zone of apprehension, Pujara withdraws his bat, covers the line and makes a watchful leave.
Bouncer angling down leg, no way Pujara has anything to do with that one.
Off the inside portion of the bat. Kohli uses the angle into him to flick, does so and places it just wide of short mid-wicket. A single is collected.
Cutting back in from outside off, met with the full face of the bat.
Stays a little low as Hazlewood serves it outside off on a length, Kohli taps it off the bottom half of the bat towards cover-point. Wants the run but doesn't decide to take it in the end.
On the sixth stump line, coming back in, Kohli walks a step across, covers the line and shoulders arms.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Stays back and keeps it out with the full face of the bat.
Bumper from the pacer, ducked and evaded.
Fraction straight in line, defensively pushed on the leg side.

Big shout for a leg before, but it's turned down. Height the issue? Probably going down leg too. Replays confirm the same, so good call from Ian Gould. Pat Cummins though, he's been excellent. Bending his back and troubling the Indian batsmen. He lands it on middle and leg and it keeps going down, raps Pujara high on the thigh pad as he fails to put bat on ball.
Good length delivery in the off stump channel, blocked with soft hands on the off side.

Pujara takes the pull shot on and ironically, to his good fortune, that saves him, because there's a man in the deep. Short ball angling in, it's pulled over backward square without much timing. It falls well short of the fielder in the deep and a single is taken.
Gets right behind the line of this one, hangs a straight bat out and defends it in front of short mid-wicket.
Keeps it in the channel outside off, Che stands firm and keeps it out on the off side.
Sharp bouncer, the batsman ducks comfortably under it.

FOUR! That's a well-earned boundary for Cheteshwar Pujara. Overpitched delivery around off, right in the slot for Pujara who doesn't think twice about whacking it away. Hammers it past mid off all the way to the fence. Super shot.
Length delivery which rises off the surface, Pujara hangs back and pushes it towards the cover area.
Fuller length ball and it's pushed towards short extra cover for no run.

Almost dragged it on! Pat Cummins is on fire. Could have has his third, that too of the Indian skipper. Good length delivery with some good pace on it, Kohli looks to defend but there's some slight nip inside. It takes the inside edge and whiskers past the leg stump. A couple of runs are taken.
Plays it very late. Length ball on off, Kohli hangs his bat ahead of him and blocks.
Too far outside off, Kohli takes a step outside, covers the line and leaves it alone.
In the off stump channel from Cummins, no shot offered by the batsman.
Fullish in length and shaping away from outside off, left alone.
Short length ball on middle and leg, Pujara keeps it out to mid-wicket. Maiden over.
Wider outside off, the batsman mistimes his attempted cut to gully on the bounce.
Fuller in legnth and slightly coming in after landing, Pujara comes ahead to defend. Again catches the inner half of the bat and the ball rolls onto the leg side.
Defends this length one off the middle of the bat this time onto the leg side.
Outside off this time, Che tries to defend from within the crease. He gets a thick inner edge that goes onto his pads.
Length ball on off stump, Pujara pushes the ball to mid-wicket.
Josh Hazlewood to bowl from the other end.
Kohli off the mark straightaway, fuller length and on middle. He takes a huge stride down and pushes the ball to the left of mid on for a couple.

The players and umpires are back for the final session of play. About 35 overs are left to be bowled today. Virat Kohli joins Cheteshwar Pujara in the middle. Kohli will be on strike facing Pat Cummins, who has one delivery to go in this over.
... Day 1, Session 3 ...

A tiring session for Australia, but that late wicket of Mayank Agarwal will have given them much to smile about. 66 runs were scored in 26.5 overs, with the Aussies having to toil hard, but Pat Cummins' late breakthrough has sort of brought them back into this game. Agarwal was playing well, scoring a finely-crafted fifty on debut, but was eventually undone by the short ball. There's plenty of batting left to come from the Indians, but the hosts would feel they can use this opportunity to make further inroads. Join us for the final session in a short while.

OUT! GOT 'EM! Pat Cummins has struck gold. It's his second of the innings and it's the short ball which does the trick once more. Short ball a bit down the leg side, Agarwal looks to fend it away awkwardly, but the ball brushes the gloves and Tim Paine behind the stumps takes it well by moving to his left. Initially Mayank doesn't walk, stands there as the Australians appeal, but eventually umpire Ian Gould raises his finger and gives him his marching orders. A good knock though from the opener comes to an end. TEA ON DAY 1!
Back of a length and on off, Agarwal is up for this as he taps it down on the off side.
Wide outside off, it is left alone for the keeper to collect.

Edged and FOUR! First false shot from Mayank all day. Full and well outside off, he's just drawn into it and a thick edge is induced. Much to his fortune though, it flies wide of the slip cordon and races away to the third man boundary. Frustration for the Australians.
A little short, kept out safely by the batsman.
Works it off his pads but finds the fielder on the leg side.
Stays very, very low. Well done, Pujara, for keeping that at bay. Length ball which goes at knee height, the batsman defends it from the toe end.
Opens the face slightly and ends up driving it a bit square towards cover-point.
This full delivery outside off is driven to the left of mid off. Wanted the single at first but is then sent back.
Keeps a little low as Marsh pitches it on middle, Pujara defends from the inner portion in front of square leg. No run taken.
Good length delivery on middle and off, Che stands firm and blocks it under his nose.
Cummins attacks the stumps, but the opener drives it to mid on by bringing down a straight bat.
Fullish delivery, just outside off, a punchy-push is played as the ball finds cover-point.
That wasn't exactly far away. Pat with a length ball around off and it jags back in, Agarwal leaves it alone but it's a little too close for comfort.
Well outside off, no way the batsman troubles himself with that.

FOUR! The timing on it is fantastic. Full ball outside off, Agarwal nicely leans into the shot and drives it through the covers. Lyon chases after it, tries to pull it back in with a dive but just can't. His hand touches the rope while doing so and he himself signals to the umpire that it's a boundary. Fair play to him.
Coming in at first and then shaping away late, Agarwal is a little squared up as he defends it under his nose.
Slightly behind a good length, Pujara ends the over without any damage.
Full ball on the stumps and it is driven to mid on.
On a length on the stumps, blocked out solidly from within the crease.

Pujara survives a massive scare! First sign of some life for the Aussies. Marsh brings it back in on middle and Pujara hangs his bat out to play. It takes the inside edge, lobs off the thigh pad and falls agonizingly short of Usman Khawaja at gully who comes running in and dives forward to try and take it.
Straighter in line, worked away on the leg side.
Full ball on off stump, defended from the inner half in front of square on the leg side.
Almost... almost. That was close. Cummins makes this go away late after serving it on a length around off, Agarwal fishes for it and nearly nicks it behind.
Well played. There wasn't much room on offer once more, but Agarwal managed to find the gap. Placed this behind point with a little dab and came back for the second.
Four dots in a row. Short and on off, Agarwal rises up on his toes and defends it with soft hands on the off side.
Cummins isn't giving anything away easily. Keeps it on off and it cuts back in, Mayank defends from inside his crease.
Short of a good length on off, tight line again, the batsman gets on top of the bounce and blocks.
Length ball on the fourth stump line, Agarwal can only defend it away towards gully.
Short of a length in line of the stumps, Pujara goes on the back foot and punches it past the bowler. Mid on moves to his left and cuts it off.
On a length this time, some extra bounce on offer, the ball is met with the full face of the bat.
Back of a length on the stumps, blocked.
Brings his wrists into play as he flicks this one angling into him through square leg for a single.
Outside off this time, Mayank pushes it tamely in front of covers.
Marsh keeps it nice and tight as he bowls a length ball on off, Mayank with a defensive shot in response.
Change of ends for Mitchell Marsh.
On the fifth stump line, Cummins giving little room as it's coming back in, the batsman defends with a straight blade in response.
Some extra bounce off the surface, a length ball on off, Pujara takes his bottom hand off as he blocks it.
Short ball banged in, Pujara ducks and evades.
Touch straight in line, slightly fullish in length, it's flicked through the vacant mid-wicket area for a double.
Rising from the surface as it's landed on a length, Cheteshwar is watchful as he keeps it out safely.

Quick single taken, good running between the wickets. Agarwal pushes this fuller length ball towards mid off and takes off. There is a shy at the bowler's end which misses, but Mayank would have been in even if a direct hit would have been scored.
Pat Cummins returns to the attack.
Makes use of the feet, gets close to the pitch and pushes it away.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Leans ahead into the full ball and knocks it wide of mid on for a run.
Fullish in length again, kept out solidly.
Some drift away, fuller in length, Mayank is well forward in defense.

SIX! The first one of the innings and Agarwal has decided to go after Lyon. Probably the best way to play against the GOAT. Tossed up on the stumps, Mayank gives the charge, goes with the spin and slogs it over cow corner for a biggie.
Agarwal uses the angle into him and flicks it to deep square leg for one run.
On the fuller side of the length, guarded out safely from the front foot.
Full and straight, driven back in the bowler's direction.
Keeps low again, a length ball on off, Agarwal does well to defend it with a straight bat.
Angling in on middle and leg, pushes to the man positioned at mid on.
Room offered outside off as Marsh lands it on a good length. Agarwal opens the face and dabs it towards the tumbling gully fielder.
Flighted delivery and it's driven towards deep mid on for a single.
Agarwal comes forward and pushes it back down the track.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
This one kept low. Lyon bowls it shorter in line of the stumps, Agarwal does well to deal with the low bounce.
Quite straight in line, full in length, worked away gently on the leg side.
Floats it right up there, on middle and leg, wristed away towards wide mid on.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman and that will be the end of this Mitchell Marsh over.
Marsh keeps it marginally short once more, Pujara again is rock solid in defense.
Stays right behind the line of this one and blocks it out.
Too straight in line, Agarwal clips this in front of square leg and gets to the other end. The 100 comes up for India with this.
Just behind a length, close to the off stick, Mayank keeps it out from the back foot.
Length delivery outside off, left alone for the keeper to collect.
Mitchell Marsh replaces Mitchell Starc.
Seeing Pujara give the charge, Lyon fires it full on the stumps. Che somehow manages to keep it at bay.
FOUR! Played that very late and the timing on that is superb. Pujara hangs back to this shorter ball outside off, waits for it, uses the pace and unleashes the cut behind point for a boundary.
Darts this one on middle and leg, Mayank goes on the back foot and clips it into the leg side. A single is taken.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Tossed up outside off, Pujara uses his feet to skip down and drives it through the empty spaces in the covers. Three runs are collected.
Quicker and straighter outside off, full in length, Pujara defends it off the inner half towards square leg.
Shaping back in on middle and leg, worked away square on the leg side. Dot ball as it's straight to the fielder.

Back of a length delivery outside off, Pujara stays on the back foot and slaps it through the gap in the covers. Takes three runs and that brings up the 50-run stand between these two. Been a very good one till now.
Back of a length ball angling in on off, Che stays perfectly behind the line and blocks it out.
Fires this in full and on off, drilled straight to mid off.
Sprays it on the pads, easily flicked away by Pujara for a couple of good runs.
Comes running in and lands it on a length outside off, Pujara covers the line and leaves it alone.
Pushes this tossed up delivery to the left of the bowler, but Nathan Lyon moves swiftly and stops the ball.
Drifting away from around off, fuller in length, Agarwal defends without any trouble.
Plants his front foot forward and presents the full face of the bat.
Agarwal moves inside the line and nudges it towards short fine leg.
Quicker and shorter on leg stump, defended down with soft hands.
Darted on leg, Mayank picks it off his pads and works it away on the leg side.

Drinks have been summoned by the umpires. A clean hour for the Indians, frustrating the Aussies bowlers. Lyon is on from one end now, but hasn't looked the Lyon of the first two games so far. Can they continue, or will the Aussies break this stand in the next hour?

Beaten! Short ball on off stump that just reverses a tad bit after landing. Pujara who was looking to play at it, is just beaten on the outside in the end. Good way to end the over from the left-arm quick.
Short length ball outside off, Pujara keeps it out on the off side.
Effort delivery outside off, left alone by the batsman.
Inside edge! But safe as it goes onto the pads. Fuller length outside off, Pujara goes for a drive but the ball takes the inside edge and goes onto the pads.
Short of a length ball outside off, Che pushes it towards the cover fielder.
Outside off, left alone by Pujara.
Flatter and quicker to end the over, Agarwal comes ahead and dead-bats.
Shorter this time, Mayank in his crease keeps it out with the straight bat.
Flatter delivery on middle, Agarwal drives it back to Lyon.
Full ball on off, defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

Flatter ball from around the wicket, Agarwal misses his flick and gets hit in line it seems. The ball may have just pitched outside leg and that is what makes the umpire say no. The Aussies appeal for a lot of time but do not go upstairs. The Ball Tracker confirms that the ball was pitching outside leg.
Looped up outside off, Pujara has his dancing shoes on as he works this away to deep mid-wicket and gets to the other end.
Another short length delivery coming in with the angle, Agarwal defends it from within his crease.
Bouncer! The batsman sways out of the way and evades the ball.
Very full and slightly wide outside off, Agarwal pushes the ball to the cover fielder on a bounce.
Another length ball on top of off stump, compact looking defensive shot from Mayank towards cover.
Shorter outside off, Agarwal pushes the ball to point off his back foot.
Fuller outside off, Agarwal comes ahead and drives but the ball finds the cover fielder.
Mitchell Starc is back into the attack. Will begin from around the wicket.
Flatter ball from over the wicket, Pujara takes a big stride ahead and he keeps it out towards the point fielder.
Fuller ball on middle, pushed to long on and Agarwal gets to the other end.
Flatter ball on off and middle, Mayank comes ahead to defend and the ball goes off the inner half of the bat on to the leg side.
Around the wicket now, pushed back to the bowler on the front foot.
Flatter ball on middle, Agarwal stands in his crease and tries to work it away on the leg side but finds short leg.
Over the wicket, looped up outside off, Pujara comes down the track and flicks it away to deep square leg for a single.
A bumper from Hazlewood, it's sharp and accurate on middle. Agarwal just about manages to evade it.
Short ball on middle and off, Agarwal rises on his toes and defends it down with gentle hands.
Picked off by Pujara. Bread and butter stuff for him. On the pads, he just flicks this through backward square leg and takes three.
In the channel outside off, left alone by the batsman.
Keeps it close to off, on a length, blocked from within the crease.
Length delivery on off stump, Pujara responds with a straight bat in defense.

FOUR! There's his fifty! Maiden one and that too, on debut in a Boxing Day Test at the MCG. Couldn't be better. Fuller ball and Agarwal hops down the track and hits it to the left of Lyon, all the way to the long off boundary. It has been a good innings so far but he needs to continue, there is a big one waiting for him out there.
Flatter ball on middle, Agarwal defends it back down the ground off the back foot.
Shorter in length, Agarwal rocks back and pushes it to short leg.
Flatter outside off this time, Mayank pushes it to cover.

FOUR! Catch it is the call but the ball is well above the head of mid off and goes all the way for a boundary. Flighted ball on middle, Agarwal dances down the track but is not quite to the pitch of the ball. He goes through with the shot and manages to lift the ball above mid off, albeit not convincingly. Moves to 49!
Flighted on off and turning slightly after landing, Agarwal comes ahead and defends the ball.
Nathan Lyon is back into the attack.
Bouncer but the line is well outside off, left alone by the Indian number 3.
Wider outside off and left alone by the batsman. Good carry on this one to Paine.
Shorter ball outside off, Pujara stands tall and defends it into the ground.
Fuller length ball on middle, CP comes ahead and defends it back down the ground.
Length ball on top of off stump, Pujara keeps it out towards mid-wicket.
Short length ball at the hips, nudged towards fine leg off the thigh pad. A leg bye is taken.

FOUR! The patience of Cummins seems to have gotten over here. He overpitches and Pujara latches onto it in a flash. He drives it beautifully all the way for a boundary through the covers. First runs for Pujara after Lunch. Good over for India, 7 runs off it.
Slightly fuller this time, Che pushes it softly towards the point fielder.
Outside off on a length, Pujara defends it holding his shape.

Length and outside off, once more Mayank prods ahead and uses the pace of Cummins to push this ball in the gap between point and gully. Lyon, who gives chase, fumbles the ball while picking it up and allows the batsmen to collect three runs.
Bouncer! Agarwal ducks underneath the ball and lets it go.
Outside off and left alone by the batsman.
Dot to end the over. The ball is on a length outside off and Pujara plays it with delicate hands and drops the ball on the pitch.
Short length ball on middle and leg, the batsman gets inside the line and tucks it down to fine leg for a single.
Well outside off, Agarwal pushes this ball off the back foot and in the gap to the left of point for a couple. Gets into the 40s.
Wide outside off, pushed on the front foot towards the left of cover. The fielder moves to the left and stops it, preventing the single.
Short and outside off, Agarwal is on top of the bounce as he keeps this out on the off side.
Length ball on middle and Mayank stands tall as he defends this.
Length ball on middle that is watchfully defended. Another maiden over.
Full and outside off, Pujara gets the ball ping off the middle of the bat and back to mid on.
Bouncer aimed at the head of the batsman, he just shrugs and moves out of the way of the cherry.
Down the leg side, Pujara must've felt like he missed out there as he doesn't connect his flick.
Full yet again, Che doesn't time his front foot drive too well as he tries to beat mid off to his right.
Full and just outside off, Pujara comes ahead and defensively pushes it back to mid off.
Fuller to end the over, Mayank pushes it to cover. Dot ball and a maiden. Second on the trot.
Good length ball outside off and coming in after landing. Agarwal gauges the line, length and movement before he leaves the ball. Good cricket all around.
Some chin music for the batsman, he lets that bouncer through to the wicket keeper.
Solid defensive shot this time to a length ball on middle.

Good ball! Takes the outside edge after bouncing off a length outside off. Agarwal does well to remove his bottom hand and ensure the ball does not carry to Aaron Finch at second slip. Finchy dives to his right and stops the ball.
Length ball coming into the body, Agarwal keeps it out towards the mid on fielder.
Wider outside off to end the over, left alone by the batsman. Good over by Cummins, a maiden.
Such a straight bat offered in defense! Lovely to watch. Full ball and pushed right back down the ground.
Length ball outside off, the batsman is not tempted.
Full and making the batsman play yet again, Che pushes it out towards cover-point.
Full and wide outside off and it is left alone by the batsman.
Fuller length on middle, Pujara turns it away towards the mid-wicket fielder.
Pat Cummins to bowl from the other end after Lunch.
Bouncer going down leg, left alone.
Fuller and outside off, Mayank comes ahead and punches it towards cover.
Fuller and pushed wide of mid on. Agarwal has a loud call of no as he sends Pujara back.

Cut him in half there! The length ball outside off, comes in with the angle and Agarwal is a bit late to bring down his willow. The ball goes right through and luckily for him, also above the off stump.
Short of a length ball on middle, kept out off the back foot towards mid-wicket.

FOUR! Lovely shot to begin the session. Full and a half-volley outside off from Hazlewood, Agarwal leans into the booming drive and gets it in the gap. The ball is a little slow as it is about to reach the cover fence but eventually just makes it. Good start for the visitors in the second session.

The two batsmen are followed by the bowling team as they make their way back onto the field of play. Should be an intriguing session of play, Mayank Agarwal to take strike first up. Josh Hazlewood to bowl the first over after Lunch.
... Day 1, Session 2 ...

For the hosts, the stand-out bowler will have to be Pat Cummins. Actually he has been the only one to have extracted some help from the wicket, albeit by bowling short and aiming the bouncers well. He picked up the only wicket to fall as well. The rest have looked a bit rusty and will have to come back better after Lunch. That being said, they haven't given too many runs away and won't be entirely disappointed. The pitch does look a good one to bat on and one would suppose it could be a good toss to win as we even saw a couple of balls keep low, not carry through in the first session of a game. What is in store ahead? Come back and join us for the post-Lunch session to find out.

A good session for India. Would have been even better if they hadn't lost the wicket of a very patient Hanuma Vihari, who played 66 balls for his 8 runs. He could argue that he did the job of seeing the new ball out but there was a great chance to get a big score out there with not too many demons in the wicket. Cheteshwar Pujara, who came to replace him, has looked really solid so far. But the man of the session will definitely have to go to Mayank Agarwal, who in his debut in a Boxing Day Test at the MCG has played really calm and sensible cricket. He has gotten himself to 34 and will be very pleased with the way things have gone so far. Looked comfortable against both pace and spin.
Another dot ball to end the over and it is a maiden. That will be LUNCH ON DAY 1 OF THIS THIRD TEST. INDIA ARE 57/1!
Length ball on middle and shaping away slightly. Pujara has no difficulty defending towards the off side.
Very full on this occasion, the batsman comes ahead to keep this ball out.
On middle and leg once more, Pujara with a straight bat gets it towards the same fielder.
Another length ball, this time on middle. Che defends it towards mid-wicket.
Length ball on off stump, pushed towards cover.
Fuller this time, defended on the front foot towards cover.

Ouch! Another one on the body for Agarwal. Short of a length and coming in. Mayank tries to sway away but can't get out of the line of the ball and gets hit. Lots of bruises but that cannot cause you to lose concentration.
Fuller outside off, Pujara comes ahead and drives with an open face of the willow. The ball runs in the gap to the left of point. It doesn't reach the fence but the batsmen can pick up three runs.
Fuller outside off, defended into the ground on the off side.
Well outside off and coming in slightly late, left alone by Che after he gauges the line and length.
Short of a length on middle, Pujara misses his flick and gets hit on the thigh pad. The ball is too high to be hitting the stump and the fielding team doesn't appeal.
Josh Hazlewood to replace Mitchell Starc.
Good end to the over from MM, Agarwal keeps out the length ball towards point.
At the hips and on a length, turned away for a single to deep square leg.
Full and wide outside off, Pujara is not drawn into a shot.
On off and middle, flicked away towards mid-wicket but no run available.
Beaten! Good ball outside off and Che who was trying to feel the ball is beaten as it moves away slightly after landing.
Length ball going down leg. Pujara misses his flick and gets hit on the pads. But the Aussies know that the ball was well down leg stump and don't appeal.
Short length ball outside off, played well defensively by Mayank towards cover.
Bouncer to Agarwal, he climbs on top of the bounce and defends it back down the ground.
Dropped with soft hands on the off side and a quick single is taken.
Another bouncer that comes in slightly after landing, Che moves away from the line of the ball. But his eyes are always on the ball at all times.
Short of a length again but this doesn't bounce that much. Pujara defends towards mid-wicket.
Bouncer which is wide down the leg side, left alone.
Outside off and kept out towards the point fielder to end the over.
Length ball on middle, Agarwal shows the full face of the bat and defends.

Loud appeal! This one has kept low and the Aussies are asking the question. A length ball on middle and Agarwal jumps to defend it. The ball keeps low and Mayank almost misses his defensive push. But the ball has come off the under part of the bat and then gone on to hit the pad. The umpire is unmoved and the home team decides not to go upstairs.
Drifts onto the pads and there is an easy single on offer as the batsman works it away to deep backward square leg.
Length ball on middle, Pujara is half-ahead and pushes it to short mid on.
A single down to deep point to begin the over. Length ball outside off, pushed by Agarwal for a run.
6 out of 6. The batsman just fends it off towards the backward square leg fielder. Dot ball.
5th straight short of a length delivery. This is wide outside off stump and Pujara decides to let it go.
Definite plan this! Another short length ball on middle, Agarwal turns it away on the leg side towards mid-wicket and gets to the other end. 50 up for the visitors. Has been a solid start so far.
Short length for the third ball in a row, Pujara hops and turns it around towards fine leg for a run.
Almost a half-tracker but aimed at the body this time. CP stands tall and plays it with very soft hands.
Bouncer first up, but Pujara moves out of the way easily.
Mitchell Starc is back for his second spell. A very fine third man in place.
Short of a length ball on off and middle, Agarwal pushes it back to the bowler.

Outside off on a length and Pujara gets off the mark with a good shot towards deep backward point. The ball is wide enough for Che to cut and he plays it very late after getting on top of the bounce. Three runs till the ball is thrown back.
Angling down on the pads, worked away to the fine leg fielder for a single.
On middle again, he stands tall and defends this with a straight bat.
Short seems to be the length to be hitting on this surface. This ball suddenly rises just that extra bit and gets Mayank on the glove. Thankfully for him, it just falls onto the ground.
Short of a length and aimed at the hips, Mayank fends it away towards the mid-wicket fielder.
Outside off, kept out pretty comfortably. Maiden over.
Bouncer, angling down leg. Che adjusts well and sways out of the way of the delivery.
Good ball just outside off and slightly short of a length, Pujara lets the ball go pretty late.
Length ball on off, Pujara comes ahead and defends it back down the ground.
Outside off stump on a length, Che defends the ball with soft hands.
Very full on middle and Pujara tries to turn it around on the leg side but finds the mid-wicket fielder.
Length ball on middle to end the 20th over. Agarwal keeps it out off the back foot.
Goes full again and drifts onto the pads. Agarwal flicks it wristily towards deep mid-wicket for another couple.
Length ball on middle and off, Agarwal defends it into the ground.
Another short of a length delivery to which Mayank just presents a straight bat from within the crease.
Length ball outside off stump, defended off the back foot on the off side.
Fuller on the pads to start off with, flicked away by Agarwal for a couple.
Mitchell Marsh has been called onto bowl for the first time today.
A bouncer to welcome Pujara, the batsman just lets it go.
Cheteshwar Pujara is in at number 3, replacing Hanuma Vihari.

OUT! Caught! The first one is gone and the short ball has done the trick! It was the only ball that was causing trouble so far. Cummins had hit the batsmen twice so far and the bouncers were well-directed. This one was perfect too. Vihari, who took his eyes off the ball, was trying to duck but couldn't get his gloves out of the way. The ball lobbed up to Finch, who ran to his right from second slip and took a very easy catch. Good effort bowling that from Cummins, need that on this kind of a wicket.
Back to the off stump line and Hanuma is content to push it to cover this time.
Drifting onto middle and leg, Vihari turns it around the corner towards deep square leg. Picks up a comfortable couple.
Slightly short of a length outside off, he pushes it towards short cover.
Length ball outside the off stump, Vihari is half-ahead in defense.
Another dot to end the over. The ball is looped up on middle, Mayank takes a stride forward and defends.
Flatter delivery outside off, Agarwal defends watchfully.
Flatter ball on the pads, Vihari gets inside the line and whips it away for a single to deep square leg.
Another quicker one with the angle, HV dead-bats it.
Slightly looped up, Vihari comes down the track and pushes it towards mid-wicket.
Flatter ball, angling away outside the off stump as Lyon comes from around the wicket. Vihari defends it into the ground.
Length ball at the hips, Mayank flicks it away but it goes straight towards short mid-wicket.
Bouncer going down leg, Agarwal wants nothing to do with it.

Overthrows here and unnecessary from the Aussies. Length ball on off stump and Vihari keeps it out to mid-wicket. Finch fires in a wild throw back to Paine that the keeper can't collect and the batsmen can run through for an overthrow.
Bouncer! Well outside the off stump though. The batsman sways out of the way.
Length delivery served just outside off, Hanuma is confident in defense.
Short of a length ball outside off, kept out by Vihari on the back foot.

FOUR! Terrific shot to end the over. Similar to the first boundary he hit off the spinner. Wide outside off, Agarwal frees his arms and drives it hard in the gap and the ball races away to the cover fence.
Fuller in length and slightly flighted, driven to mid on.
Shorter in length, pushed away to long on off the back foot for a single.
Quicker, drilled in on middle, Hanuma comes ahead and defends it back to the bowler.
Flatter ball on middle, Vihari comes down the ground to defend. Seems to have hit his pad first and there is a huge appeal. The Aussies think about the review but decide not to, in the end.
Looped up outside off, Vihari plays his 50th ball into the ground on the off side.

Drinks are on the field. And India haven't lost a wicket so far. This is by far their best opening show in the series. Agarwal has looked positive on debut and Vihari is as solid as you'd expect him to be, so the move to start things off with these two has paid off for India, so far. The Australians, the pacers in particular, need to better their lengths. Should be going fuller instead of bowling short on this opening day of the Boxing Day Test. Pretty sure Justin Langer will have sent that message down during this break.
Shaping away from outside off, tapped away towards cover-point.
Slightly short again, another easy block from Mayank.
Marginally behind a length, on middle and off, defended from inside the crease.
Another cracker from Cummins. It's not that short again, but he hits the deck hard at 143 clicks, Agarwal makes the mistake of taking his eyes off the ball and cops a blow on the shoulder.
Sharp. Cummins is generating some good pace here. Angling in on leg and it shoots off the deck a bit, Agarwal is caught high on the thigh pad as he looks to play at it.
On a good length on off, Agarwal is a bit squared up as he defends it from within the crease.
Just behind a driving length, on off, Vihari lunges forward, gets close to the pitch and blocks it out well.
Floated in line of the stumps, kept out with a straight blade.
Is well forward to this tossed up ball as he pushes it away defensively to covers.
Touch short in length again, on middle and leg this time, Vihari goes back and turns it to short leg.
Quicker one outside off, shorter in length too, the batsman goes on the back foot and defends it down on the off side.
Looped up around leg, Vihari uses his feet to come down the track. Looks to flick but is caught on the pads.
In much better control of this one. Agarwal taps this length ball down in front of cover-point to end the over.
Coming in at first but then it straightens off the seam, around off, played off the outer half square on the off side.
Zipping off the deck, a length ball outside off, Mayank covers the line and lets it go through.

The physio is out to have a look at Hanuma Vihari. He looks okay, but you never want to take any chances with head injuries. A new helmet has been called for too. He seems fine, which is a good sign. Nice to see.

That's nasty! Cummins has caught Vihari on the helmet. That was a big noise as the ball struck the helmet. Not that short as Vihari looks to duck, looks to get under it but it goes off the helmet and bounces towards square leg. The batsmen take a leg bye.
Angles this full ball into the batsman, Agarwal flicks it wide of mid on and crosses over.
Full delivery on off stump, driven hard by Mayank but straight to mid off.
Second change for Australia. Pat Cummins is called into action.
Good stop from Lyon. Vihari offers a full-blooded drive towards mid on, but the offie moves to his right and stops it well.
Flighted delivery on middle and leg, Hanuma gets his front leg out of the way and defends.
Another defensive shot. No run taken.
Moving away from around off, pushed off the outer half on the off side.
Full and straight, on the stumps, kept out by coming well forward.
Drifting away from around the wicket, Agarwal plays it off the outer half towards cover-point. Both batsmen are alert and change ends easily. Well done.
Targets the top of off stump, the batsman gets behind the line and keeps it out.
Hanuma opens the face of the bat, waits for it to come to him before dabbing it to gully.
Straightening up after landing on off, guarded out from within the crease.
More runs for Vihari. Angling in on off, Hanuma plays it with the angle as he flicks it wide of short mid-wicket. Easy two for him.
Bumper outside off, Hanuma picks up the line early and sways away from the ball.
This full length delivery is driven down the ground towards mid off.
A bit quicker through the air, on off stump, Agarwal defends it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
The off break on middle and off, defended well off the front foot by the batsman.
Darts it across the right-hander, it's pushed into the covers. Dot ball.
Plants his front foot forward and drives it straight to the mid off fielder.
Some flight on this, it's spinning in on leg, Agarwal safely deals with it.
Quicker one on off from around the wicket, met with a straight bat in response.
Josh keeps it full once more, Vihari positions himself behind the line and drives it with the full face to the man at mid on.
Drives this one to the covers, can't find the gap though as the fielder moves swiftly to his left to cut it off.
Sharp bouncer from Hazlewood, on middle, Hanuma keeps his eyes on the ball and arches back to let it sail over his head.
Full again, Vihari presents a straight bat in defense and keeps it out.
Full in length, on middle and off, blocked from the front foot.
Cutting back in off the seam, a good length delivery, goes off Vihari's pads and falls on the leg side as he misses his flick shot.
Change of ends for Josh Hazlewood.
FOUR! Shot. That's well in the gap this time. Too full and too wide outside off, Agarwal drills it through the covers for a boundary.
Good stop from Travis Head. Agarwal drives it firmly, looking to find the gap in the covers, but Head dives to his right and stops it.
And Hanuma Vihari is off the mark after 24 balls. He drives this tossed up ball down towards deepish mid on and gets to the other end. He will be relieved with that.
Tossed up outside off, it's the straighter one, Hanuma takes a big stride forward and defends.
Spinning in on middle and off, driven back down the track for nothing.
Tossed up outside off, Vihari drives but straight to the man at cover.
Already spin introduced. Nathan Lyon is brought into the attack in the 8th over itself.
Good length delivery, aiming the top of off stump, guarded out safely from within the crease.
Brings it in closer, but still down leg, Agarwal looks to flick but misses.
FOUR BYES! No bounce at all on this once. Wow. It was a bit short down the leg side, but it almost goes along the turf and past Tim Paine for another boundary.

FOUR! Goes after this one and almost pays the price for it. Just away from Mitchell Marsh at gully. Couldn't resist the temptation this time as Agarwal reaches out for this full delivery wide outside off, gets a thick edge and it flies inches over a diving Marsh. It races away to the fence for a boundary.
Short but way down the leg side, no reason for the batsman to go after it.
Angling away from a length, around off, Mayank moves a step across, gets behind the line and blocks.
Excellent timing but still no run for Hanuma Vihari. He drives it down the ground, but mid on moves to his left and cuts it off with a dive.
Hazlewood comes from wide of the crease and spears it in full on the stumps, Vihari takes a step forward and drives it, only to find mid on.
Bumper in line of the stumps, angling in, Vihari gets right behind the line and blocks it down on the leg side.
Shortish delivery on off stump, defended back out off the back foot.

Vihari isn't off the mark yet, but he's doing a fine job of sticking it out in the middle. Important for him not to lose his cool in search of that run. He drives this full delivery back to Hazlewood.
Angling in on off, fullish in length, Hanuma works it towards short mid-wicket.
Back of a length on middle and leg, worked down in front of short leg to end the over.
Another confident shot from Agarwal. He's looking fearless here. He comes forward to this full ball and offers a firm punch through the covers. Gets two more to his name.
Too straight in line once more, not much swing for Starc, it's turned through backward square leg for a brace.

That's a ripper from Starc, equally well played by Mayank Agarwal too. It's short, sharp and accurate, going away from the batsman. Agarwal is on the front foot initially, goes back and does well to drop his hands to avoid that.
Fraction straight in line, Mayank works it away behind square leg and comes back for the second.
Full in length, outside the line of off stump, driven to the man at cover.
Full, straight and on the stumps, hit straight back in the bowler's direction.
Just beaten. That's a good delivery. Angles in at first but then nips away ever so slightly off the seam. Vihari is drawn forward and he almost nicks it.
Outside off on a good length, arms are shouldered to this one.

Lovely timing on that. Mayank Agarwal waits for it as the ball comes in full and too straight in line, he flicks it through mid-wicket with good balance. Marsh chases it down, but the batsmen get three runs.
Lands it a bit wide of off stump, the batsman makes a safe leave.
Fullish in length, just around off, Mayank defends it from the front foot.
On the shorter side of the length, Vihari remains on the back foot as he deals with it well.
Oooooh! There is a short leg in place and Vihari almost falls prey to it. Starc bangs it in short and into the body, Hanuma awkwardly fends it away and it falls just short of the close-in fielder.
Moving away late from around off, a good length delivery, Hanuma covers the line and lets it be.
Quite full again, in line of the stumps, blocked back down the track solidly.
Short of a length into the body, nudged fine down the leg side for a single.
Well played. Safely kept out by Mayank Agarwal. Looks quite confident, which is good to see. Starc fires in a yorker on the stumps, Mayank brings his bat down and keeps it at bay.
Rising off the deck once again, outside off, left alone to end the over.
Nice and straight from Hazlewood, Vihari can't do much more than block it out.

First runs of the morning and this Test match. First runs for Mayank Agarwal in Test cricket and the huge Indian support in the crowd gives him a big round of applause. Full and outside off, Agarwal takes a good stride forward and plays a punchy-drive through the covers for three runs.
Nice carry for Hazlewood. He serves it outside off on a length and it rises off the deck, Mayank makes a watchful leave.
Hazlewood goes full and attacks the stumps, Agarwal is well forward in defense.
Marginally ahead of a length, on off stump, Agarwal defends it with the full face of the bat.
Josh Hazlewood will bowl from the other end.
Hurls it outside off, pushed away towards mid off with hard hands.
Length delivery close to the off stick, defended solidly from inside the crease.
Nice shape on this as the left-arm pacer bowls it in the channel outside off, on a length, it's left alone.
Better. Keeps it full and manages to bounce it before it reaches the batsman, Hanuma Vihari defends it in front of cover by coming forward.
Second full toss in a row from Starc. This one swings back in on middle and leg, Vihari works it in front of square leg.
Fires a wide full toss outside off, Vihari reaches out to it and gets an edge which goes to the slip cordon on the bounce.

The MCG crowd is ready, we're ready, and we hope all of you out there keeping up with us and the match are too. A wonderful day with the sun shining, as Hanuma Vihari and debutant Mayank Agarwal stride out to bat. Mitchell Starc as always will take the new ball first up. Three slips and a gully in place. Here we go...
Time for the national anthems. Both teams are lined up side by side and we will begin with the visitors'.

Australia skipper, Tim Paine, says that he is happy that they will be bowling. Feels that they are happy to come in with a win and feels that it was a reward for the hard work. States that he is really proud to be captaining his country in a Boxing Day Test. Regarding the Mitchell Marsh selection, he feels that it will help the bowlers share the workload better towards the end of the series. Ends by saying that Aaron Finch is 100 percent fine and ready to go.

India skipper, Virat Kohli, feels that it is a nice hard surface under the grass covering, so would like to bat really well as it might get tougher in the 3rd and 4th innings with the surface getting slower. Doesn't feel that there is any worry about the past and is focused on the present. About the team changes, he says that they will open with Mayank Agarwal and Hanuma Vihari and wishes the former all the best for his Test debut. Regarding Rohit Sharma, he feels that Sharma could be lethal while batting with the tail and change the Test in the course of a session.
TOSS - India win the toss and elect to bat first!

Pitch report - Allan Border out in the middle feels that there is a pretty good grass covering and the conditions overhead are perfect for some Test cricket. He says that if he were the skipper of either team, he might just lean towards bowling first as the MCG wicket is traditionally known to play well and there aren't usually many terrors while batting last too.

After producing rather stale affairs on a couple of occasions, it's been said that the MCG surface is going to produce a ripper for this one. Something in it for everyone, and that's what all want to see. India took the first Test in Adelaide, but Australia made a fighting comeback in Perth. Momentum means nothing here, it all comes down to who can hold their nerve on the day. There are going to be changes on both sides, more so in the Indian camp, so it will be interesting to see what combination is fielded. Don't go anywhere, the toss is about to come up shortly.

Boxing Day brings a bittersweet feeling along with it. It will be the first time Australia have an all-Victorian opening pair in 45 years. Mayank Agarwal finally gets his call-up and what better time to make your debut. There's talk he and Hanuma Vihari will open the innings for the Indian side, and this will be the 6th opening pair for the visitors in 2018. But, along with all the good and positive news, it will be the first time in 40 years we won't have Bill Lawry on air to liven things up for everyone. Pretty sure I speak for everyone when I say this - we'll miss you, Bill!

December is the most festive time of the year, and it's a rather special one this time around - on top of it being my birthday month, Liverpool are top of the table and we have Boxing Day upon us... doesn't get much better than this, does it? A massive crowd, like every year, is expected to swarm in. The holiday season continues for the regular folk, but not for these warriors. It's long past for them and it's time to prepare for battle. There are three Tests today, but there's just something magical about the MCG. There's some added incentive to make the atmosphere more intense with the series levelled 1-1 and the winner here takes a vital lead.
